waximabbax · Nov 13, 2026

Well congrats.

Here are some thoughts not facts:

On AA Decision Index.

Decider v1.3 and Decider v.1.2 seem to have same benchmarks. However, V1.3 flash beats V1.2 flash by 4 points.

I am not particulary excited about this pattern/trend of having flash versions for decision models. The whole point of Decision models was to deliver faster ouput for high volume requests at much cheaper cost than Reasoning models. Since most reasoning models can and probably do outperform decision models already in accuracy but they are a lot slower and are pricier. Reasoning Models can already return structured ouput.

So your flagship model must be fastest and most accurate.

Unless it can handle some different form of input other than just image and text, I don't see the point of having both flagship and flash version for the same model.

declanjackson · Nov 13, 2026

deepsquirrelnet · Nov 13, 2026

> So your flagship model must be fastest and most accurate.

That's rarely the way anything in life works though. Do you prioritize fastest OR most accurate? That's a question that depends on context, task difficulty, etc.

You can use a 17M parameter NLI model for simple stuff and get orders of magnitude faster decisions. But the intelligence of that model will be quite a bit weaker.

In some tasks you might be talking about very small differences in accuracy between that model and a 27B parameter LLM decision model for several orders of magnitude in speed. In other tasks, the 17M might be about as good as a random guess.
